## Setup

```{python}
import pandas as pd
import plotly.express as px
from IPython.display import Markdown, display
import theme  # applies the "course" Plotly template

DATA_FILE = "data/jobs.csv"  # change if your cleaned dataset has a different name

cols = ["POSTED", "SALARY", "STATE_NAME", "TITLE_NAME", "SKILLS_NAME",
        "SOFTWARE_SKILLS_NAME", "REMOTE_TYPE_NAME", "MIN_YEARS_EXPERIENCE",
        "EMPLOYMENT_TYPE_NAME"]
df = pd.read_csv(DATA_FILE, usecols=cols, low_memory=False)
df["POSTED"] = pd.to_datetime(df["POSTED"], errors="coerce")
df["MONTH"] = df["POSTED"].dt.to_period("M").astype(str)
print(f"{len(df):,} postings loaded")
```

## Job Postings Over Time

```{python}
monthly = (df.dropna(subset=["POSTED"])["MONTH"]
           .value_counts().sort_index().reset_index())
monthly.columns = ["Month", "Postings"]
fig = px.bar(monthly, x="Month", y="Postings", title="Job Postings by Month")
fig.show()

hi = monthly.loc[monthly["Postings"].idxmax()]
lo = monthly.loc[monthly["Postings"].idxmin()]
display(Markdown(
    f"*Interpretation: postings peak in **{hi['Month']}** ({hi['Postings']:,}) "
    f"and are lowest in **{lo['Month']}** ({lo['Postings']:,}). "
    f"Hiring activity is not constant across the period covered.*"))
```

## Most Common Job Titles

```{python}
titles = df["TITLE_NAME"].value_counts().head(10).reset_index()
titles.columns = ["Title", "Postings"]
fig = px.bar(titles.sort_values("Postings"), x="Postings", y="Title",
             orientation="h", title="Top 10 Job Titles")
fig.show()

display(Markdown(
    f"*Interpretation: the most common title is **{titles.iloc[0]['Title']}** "
    f"({titles.iloc[0]['Postings']:,} postings). The rest of the top 10 shows "
    f"that employers label this role in several different ways.*"))
```

## Salary Trends

Only postings that list a salary are included below.

```{python}
sal = df.dropna(subset=["SALARY"])
share_listed = len(sal) / len(df)
print(f"{len(sal):,} of {len(df):,} postings list a salary ({share_listed:.1%})")
sal["SALARY"].describe().round(0)
```

```{python}
fig = px.histogram(sal, x="SALARY", nbins=50,
                   title="Salary Distribution (postings with listed pay)")
fig.update_xaxes(title="Annual salary (USD)")
fig.show()
```

```{python}
fig = px.box(sal, x="MONTH", y="SALARY", title="Salary by Posting Month")
fig.update_yaxes(title="Annual salary (USD)")
fig.show()

display(Markdown(
    f"*Interpretation: the median listed salary is **${sal['SALARY'].median():,.0f}**, "
    f"with a middle 50% range of ${sal['SALARY'].quantile(0.25):,.0f} to "
    f"${sal['SALARY'].quantile(0.75):,.0f}. The maximum is "
    f"${sal['SALARY'].max():,.0f}, so outliers are present. Only "
    f"{share_listed:.1%} of postings list a salary, so these results may not "
    f"represent all postings.*"))
```

### Salary by Experience Required

```{python}
exp = sal.dropna(subset=["MIN_YEARS_EXPERIENCE"]).copy()
exp["Experience"] = pd.cut(exp["MIN_YEARS_EXPERIENCE"],
                           bins=[-1, 1, 3, 5, 8, 50],
                           labels=["0-1 yrs", "2-3 yrs", "4-5 yrs", "6-8 yrs", "9+ yrs"])
fig = px.box(exp, x="Experience", y="SALARY",
             title="Salary by Minimum Years of Experience")
fig.update_yaxes(title="Annual salary (USD)")
fig.show()

med = exp.groupby("Experience", observed=True)["SALARY"].median()
display(Markdown(
    f"*Interpretation: the median salary is ${med.iloc[0]:,.0f} for the "
    f"**{med.index[0]}** group and ${med.iloc[-1]:,.0f} for the "
    f"**{med.index[-1]}** group, so pay changes with the experience required.*"))
```

## Geographic Variation

```{python}
states = df["STATE_NAME"].value_counts().head(15).reset_index()
states.columns = ["State", "Postings"]
fig = px.bar(states.sort_values("Postings"), x="Postings", y="State",
             orientation="h", title="Top 15 States by Number of Postings")
fig.show()
```

```{python}
MIN_N = 100 if len(sal) > 5000 else 5   # smaller datasets need a lower cutoff
state_sal = (sal.groupby("STATE_NAME")["SALARY"]
             .agg(["median", "count"]).reset_index())
state_sal = state_sal[state_sal["count"] >= MIN_N].sort_values("median", ascending=False).head(15)
fig = px.bar(state_sal.sort_values("median"), x="median", y="STATE_NAME",
             orientation="h",
             title=f"Median Salary by State (states with {MIN_N}+ salary postings)")
fig.update_xaxes(title="Median annual salary (USD)")
fig.update_yaxes(title="")
fig.show()

top_post = states.iloc[0]["State"]
top_pay = state_sal.iloc[0]["STATE_NAME"]
display(Markdown(
    f"*Interpretation: **{top_post}** has the most postings, while **{top_pay}** "
    f"has the highest median salary among states with enough salary data. "
    f"{'These are the same state.' if top_post == top_pay else 'The state with the most postings is not the one that pays the most.'}*"))
```

## Remote Work

```{python}
remote = df["REMOTE_TYPE_NAME"].fillna("Unknown").value_counts().reset_index()
remote.columns = ["Type", "Postings"]
fig = px.pie(remote, names="Type", values="Postings", title="Remote vs. On-site Postings")
fig.show()

display(Markdown(
    f"*Interpretation: **{remote.iloc[0]['Type']}** is the largest category, "
    f"at {remote.iloc[0]['Postings'] / remote['Postings'].sum():.1%} of postings.*"))
```
